activities.description: Clarence introduces himself and the topic of the video: cycling in NYC during the Coronavirus crisis.
Clarence explains his plans to cycle through Manhattan and observe how New Yorkers are adapting to the pandemic.
Clarence highlights his safety precautions (maintaining social distance, touching only his bike, etc.).

scenes.contextualRelevance: The scene sets the tone for the documentary by highlighting the drastic changes in NYC due to the pandemic.

Clarence's emphasis on safety precautions reinforces the seriousness of the situation.

activities.description: Clarence departs from Queens on his bicycle.
He observes a nearly empty Long Island Railroad train.
He cycles on Skillman Avenue, noting an increase in bike activity.
He passes a park where people are exercising while maintaining social distance.

He sees an empty 7 train, another unusual sight.
He cycles on the nearly empty Queens Boulevard, highlighting the significant decrease in traffic compared to a typical morning.
He enters the Queensboro Bridge bike path, noting a lower but still present number of cyclists and pedestrians.
He observes the smooth flow of traffic on the bridge, contrasting it with typical weekday congestion.
He mentions the clean air due to reduced traffic.
He observes an almost empty Roosevelt Island Tram.

activities.description: Clarence cycles on Broadway and observes a lack of cars but an increase in cyclists, making a ratio observation.
He sees a delivery worker pushing a cart filled with packages, highlighting the increase in delivery services.
He comments on the essential role delivery workers play, especially during the pandemic.
He arrives at Union Square Greenmarket, surprised to find it still operating and serving customers.
He cycles on 14th Street and notes that the busway is even clearer than usual due to reduced traffic.
He cycles on 13th Street, observing that the bike lane is clear, only blocked by residual ice.

youtube_description:
I hadn't been on my bicycle in over a week, choosing to walk and run for exercise during the Coronavirus (and observing recommended precautions) but I was curious what my normal commute looked like. So on Friday I chose to get my exercise by bicycling in to Manhattan and brought my camera along as I visited many spots I might typically do if scouting for great locales to film footage for a Streetfilm.

The amazing thing is I have so much archives of New York City that in many cases I had exact matching footage from the last few years of each location or spot, showing what it looks like typically (or in some cases showing what it looked like before the streets received an intervention from NYC DOT) and in some cases is pretty mind blowing.

I hope this Streetfilm (likely the final "new" one shot until the world heals) is entertaining, gives you hope and stretches your mind to what is still possible when we emerge from this pandemic.
youtube_title: The Streets Have Changed: A NYC Bicycle Journey During the Coronavirus
